exact_statement: For every K>=0 and arbitrary finite disjoint uniform-cube Boolean factors, the full physical stopping hull R_K of (H-KI)_+ tensorizes exactly: R_K(product_i f_i)=sum_i R_K(f_i), with no root-sign hypothesis. Always 0<=H-R_K<=KI, and for 0<=K<=L, 0<=R_K-R_L<=(L-K)I; R_K is convex piecewise affine in K. For every actual disjoint-core Boolean composition F=B(g_i), pivotal probabilities q_i and signed correction C=H(F)-sum_i q_i H(g_i), the bank A=C+kappa I(F)+sum_i q_i R_K(g_i) satisfies H(F)+(kappa-K)I(F)<=A<=H(F)+kappa I(F). Any two representations of the same F at the same K,kappa differ by at most K I(F). With fixed kappa, unbounded A/I implies an actual ordinary H/I counterfamily, even with varying K; the converse holds at bounded K. The clipped bank A_plus=C_+ +kappa I+sum_i q_i R_K(g_i), even though not universally coherent, obeys A_plus/I-kappa<=max(H(F)/I(F),max_{i:q_i I(g_i)>0} H(g_i)/I(g_i)); its unbounded root ratio therefore extracts an actual whole-or-core Boolean counterfamily. Products cannot amplify a finite A/I or R_K/I at fixed K,kappa. For F_t the product of t independent two-bit functions negative only at00, H=2t,I=t,Var=1-4^-t,R_K=t(2-K)_+, providing sharp bank endpoints at0<=K<=2 and divergent variance/average-influence normalizations despite H/I=2. No universal initial bank bound, no full FEI proof, and no unbounded ordinary-ratio family is asserted.
hypotheses: Finite {-1,1}-valued functions on independent uniform physical bits; H is Shannon entropy in bits of the normalized squared Fourier law, I is total physical influence.
K>=0; every R_K is the true complete finite physical stopping hull, with all adaptive queries and both full outcomes retained; factors have disjoint supports.
Composition cores and outer gate are actual Boolean functions, allowing constants/dummies; q_i are actual independent biased-output pivotal probabilities, not substituted formal parameters.

Counterexample extraction uses fixed kappa, nonconstant actual whole functions, and actual full influence denominators; bounded K is required only in stated converse and representation-sequence comparisons.
